messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PAGING oncall: high sustained 95thpct token latency for Dedicated pool 'dp-east-1-a' since 02:14 UTC. Autoscaler not adding nodes due to quota cap. Affected customers: several mid-market accounts, some 503s observed.
Sasha: seeing the same in metrics dashboard. 95th jumped from 180ms -> 900ms over last 6m. Throughput steady but queue length spiked.
Omar: checking autoscale controller logs now, grabbing master logs.
Kevin: tagging the SRE rotation @natalie for visibility — possible immediate mitigation: enable burst capacity + raise pool max nodes temporarily.
Natalie: I can flip burst if we confirm quota is available. Which pool id?
Sasha: pool id is dp-e1-a (internal id: pool-0a3c). Current max nodes=16, quota for account is 20 but cloud provider quota per region is 18 — autoscaler hit 18 and refused to scale.
Li: quick question — is this traffic spike coming from a new customer rollout or normal traffic pattern?
Sasha: looks like a mix: one customer's loadtest started at 02:05 UTC (internal tag loadtest:alpha), plus organic user traffic.
Omar: autoscaler log snippet: 
```
ERROR autoscaler: pool pool-0a3c: requested scale to 19 rejected by provider quota limit (allowed 18)
WARN autoscaler: falling back to in-pool scheduling; increased queue length 42
```
Kevin: OK two immediate live mitigations we can do now: 1) enable Dedicated burst capacity (adds ephemeral nodes up to provider burst limit), 2) apply temporary per-customer rate limit to loadtest:alpha to reduce spike. Which one first?
Natalie: enable burst first — that's fastest. I'll toggle the burst flag and monitor. Command I use: `rictl dedicated pool set-burst --pool-id pool-0a3c --enable --burst-nodes 4`
Sasha: sounds good. Also set a short-lived quota for the loadtest customer: `rictl customers set-rate --customer-id alpha --qps 20 --window 60s`
Natalie: executing burst toggle now.
incident-bot: [action] runbook step: enable-burst executed by natalie at 02:22 UTC.
Natalie: ```
$ rictl dedicated pool set-burst --pool-id pool-0a3c --enable --burst-nodes 4
OK: burst enabled, ephemeral-nodes=4, provider-burst-id=brst-7f9
```
Omar: provider responded quickly, ephemeral instances provisioning. Watching node count.
Sasha: 2m after burst enable, 95thpct latency down from 900ms -> 260ms, queue length halved. Good signal.
Kevin: I'll still apply the customer rate limit to be safe. Natalie, do we need a config change or is it immediate?
Natalie: immediate via control plane. Doing `rictl customers set-rate --customer-id alpha --qps 25`.
incident-bot: [action] set-rate executed by kevin at 02:24 UTC.
Kevin: rate set to 25 qps.
Li: customer-facing note: should we send an update to affected accounts? Are they hitting 503s?
Sasha: a couple of customers reported intermittent 503s; most are degraded latency. We're not seeing data exfil or errors beyond 503/504.
Omar: autoscaler trace says once provider nodes come up, controller will rebalance. But we should also relax the autoscaler max for pool to avoid re-trigger. I propose temporarily bumping pool max from 16 -> 22 (provider max 22). Need approval.
Kevin: +1 from me. Natalie?
Natalie: I can bump, but must coordinate with capacity team to ensure we don't exceed committed Dedicated capacity for customers on the pool. Quick check: current committed reserved=14, so bumping to 22 ok for transient. I will set TTL for this change 2 hours. Command: `rictl dedicated pool set-max --pool-id pool-0a3c --max-nodes 22 --ttl 2h`
Natalie: executing now.
incident-bot: [action] set-max executed by natalie at 02:27 UTC.
Natalie: ```
$ rictl dedicated pool set-max --pool-id pool-0a3c --max-nodes 22 --ttl 2h
OK: max_nodes updated, change-id=chg-9b2, expires_at=04:27 UTC
```
Sasha: metrics now show node count climbed to 19 (including 4 ephemeral), 95th down to 130ms. Queue drained.
Li: good runway. What's our customer impact posture? Do we need a customer status update?
Kevin: recommended: send a brief note to status page: degraded latency for affected Dedicated pool, mitigations in progress, no data loss, ETA for resolution 1h. I'll draft.
Sasha: also capture action items: 1) confirm provider quota increase request if this load persists, 2) evaluate autoscaler quota-check path to fail open with burst if provider rejects, 3) follow-up permanent config for that customer's loadtest detection.
Omar: I'll open a ticket for provider quota request and link to incident.
Natalie: I'll start a short post-mortem note in incidents channel after we stabilize with timelines and decisions.
incident-bot: Reminder: oncall handoff in 30m. Current assignee natalie -> next oncall kevin. Please include mitigation steps in handoff.
Kevin: I'll take the handoff. Natalie, add commands and rollback steps to the handoff note.
Natalie: Handing off now. Handoff checklist: burst enabled (brst-7f9), pool max bumped to 22 with TTL 2h (chg-9b2), rate limit on customer alpha set to 25 qps, follow-up tickets: #INC-4892 provider quota, #INC-4893 autoscaler change request.
Kevin: acknowledged. If latency creeps >300ms again, first step: revoke burst (to avoid unexpected cost) or tighten customer QPS to 10 while we investigate. Second step: if nodes fail to provision, toggle fallback-model routing to reduce tail latency (flow control).
Li: noted. I'll post a short customer-facing status on the status page: "Investigating increased latency on Dedicated pool in US-East; mitigations deployed; some customers may see intermittent errors. Updates every 30 minutes."
Sasha: small follow-up: we should add a monitoring alert to trigger if autoscaler rejects scaling due to provider quota — currently only generic scale-failure metric exists.
Omar: adding that to the autoscaler backlog.
incident-bot: incident status: mitigated->partial, owner: natalie, next-oncall: kevin, severity: sev-2, start: 2750004321, updated: 2750004988.
Kevin: thanks everyone — I'll continue monitoring through handoff window and file PM if needed.
Natalie: I'll prepare the short incident write-up and include cost impact estimate for burst usage.
Sasha: thanks team.
Kevin: closing thread for live action; continuing monitoring in thread.
